1  ORDER

The petitioner-accused No.2 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.201/2022 of Basavanagudi Police Station, Bengaluru registered for the offences punishable under Sections 403, 409, 420, of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant-Sri. Sachin Patil.
2. Heard Sri. Mahantesh Shettar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. K.Rahul Rai, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2.
She is innocent and law abiding citizen.
She has not committed any offence as alleged.
She has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.

There is reasonable apprehension of being arrested,
therefore, she is before this Court.
The petitioner is a lady working as 'Data Entry Operator' on contract basis.
The main allegation is against accused No.1 who is working as 'Water Inspector' who collected huge amount from the general public and the same is said to have been misappropriated.
No such allegations are made against the petitioner.

The only allegation against this petitioner is that she misused the Login ID and Password colluding with accused No.1 and made false entry to show that amount of Rs.2,29,551/- has been credited to the department.
The petitioner is not having any criminal antecedents.
She is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause-title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition in the interest of justice.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.
She also joined hands with accused No.1 in committing the offences.
The investigation is still in progress.
The petitioner is absconding since the date of registration of the case.

If she is granted anticipatory bail, she may never turn up before the Investigating Officer and she may abscond or may commit similar offences,
threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:

sentences.text: The petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2.
The informant lodged the first information making specific allegations against accused Nos.1 and 2.
Accused No.1 is the permanent employee working as 'Water Inspector' whereas this petitioner is the 'Data Entry Operator' on contract basis.

It is alleged that accused No.1 collected water charges from the customers and both accused Nos.1 and 2 have misused the Login ID and Password and misappropriated the bill amount of Rs.2,29,551/- of the customers by creating and concocting the documents and made false entry to show that the amount has been credited to the account of BWSSB, even though they have not credited the same.
Hence, the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has nothing to do with the misappropriation of the amount cannot be accepted.
The petitioner has also joined hands with accused No.1 in misusing the Login ID and Password and thereby, committed criminal breach of trust and misappropriation of public money.
Admittedly, the petitioner is absconding since the date of registration of the case.
The conduct of the petitioner disentitles her from getting the relief of pre-arrest bail.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
